title: Materiality, Risk Assessment and Internal Control
outcomes: Explain components and limitations of internal control.

meta.exam_tip: Link each weakness to a COSO component and a risk, then propose a control.

concepts.title: Materiality and performance materiality (SA 320)
body: Misstatements are material if, individually or together, they could reasonably influence economic decisions of users. Materiality is a matter of judgement, considering size and nature, and is applied in planning, performing and evaluating the audit (SA 320).

Overall materiality uses a benchmark (profit before tax, revenue, total assets, equity) and a percentage suited to the entity; specific materiality applies to particular items (e.g. related party or director remuneration disclosures).
Performance materiality is set below overall materiality to reduce aggregation risk. Materiality is revised if information during the audit would have led to a different amount.
concepts.analogy: Materiality is the line between what matters and what does not.
concepts.work: A loss-making year may require revenue or assets as the benchmark.

concepts.title: Risk-based audit approach (SA 315 and SA 330)
body: Audit risk = risk of material misstatement (inherent risk × control risk) × detection risk. The auditor assesses risks at the financial statement and assertion levels through risk assessment procedures — enquiry, analytical procedures, observation and inspection — and understanding the entity, its environment, framework and internal control (SA 315).

Significant risks need special audit attention. Responses (SA 330): overall responses (team, skepticism, unpredictability) and further audit procedures — tests of controls when relying on controls, and substantive procedures for all material classes, always including substantive procedures for significant risks.
Higher assessed risk calls for more persuasive evidence: more extensive, closer to year end, and more reliable procedures.
concepts.analogy: Assess risks first, then design responses to fit them.
concepts.work: If control risk is high, detection risk must be kept low through more substantive work.

concepts.title: Internal control: nature, components and limitations
body: Internal control is the process designed and maintained by those charged with governance, management and others to provide reasonable assurance about reliable reporting, effective and efficient operations and compliance with laws.

Components: control environment, entity's risk assessment process, information system and communication, control activities (authorisation, reconciliation, verification, physical controls, segregation of duties) and monitoring of controls.
Inherent limitations: human error, collusion, management override, cost-benefit constraints and controls designed for routine transactions.
concepts.analogy: Five components work together — and none is foolproof.
concepts.work: Collusion between two employees can defeat segregation of duties.

concepts.title: Evaluating and reporting on internal control (SA 265, IFC frameworks)
body: The auditor reviews controls using narratives, flowcharts and questionnaires, evaluates design and implementation, and tests operating effectiveness where relying on them (walkthroughs, re-performance, inspection).

SA 265 requires communicating significant deficiencies in internal control in writing to those charged with governance, and other deficiencies of sufficient importance to management, on a timely basis.

Frameworks: COSO internal control framework, and in India the Companies Act requirement (section 143(3)(i)) for auditors of applicable companies to state whether internal financial controls over financial reporting are adequate and working effectively, guided by ICAI's Guidance Note.
concepts.analogy: Evaluate controls, then report weaknesses to the right people.
concepts.work: A significant deficiency must be communicated in writing to the audit committee.

illustrations.title: Setting materiality
illustrations.q: Sun Ltd. has a stable profit before tax of ₹400 lakh. The auditor uses 5% of profit before tax as overall materiality, sets performance materiality at 75% of overall materiality, and treats 5% of overall materiality as clearly trivial. Compute the three amounts and explain why performance materiality is lower.

head: Measure
Working
₹ lakh
rows: Reduces risk that aggregate uncorrected and undetected misstatements exceed overall materiality
solution.title: SA 320

checks.label: Overall materiality at 5% of profit before tax (₹ lakh)
Clearly trivial threshold at 5% of materiality (₹ lakh)

illustrations.title: Classify the control weakness
illustrations.q: Identify the internal control component affected: (a) the board never reviews ethics policies; (b) management has no process to identify new business risks; (c) one clerk both records and approves payments; (d) the ERP produces unreliable reports; (e) no one follows up on internal audit findings.

jobs.title: Risk assessment for a new client
jobs.situation: A fast-growing e-commerce company with high revenue pressure.
steps: Identify significant risks such as revenue and returns.
Evaluate key controls and IT systems.
jobs.takeaway: Materiality and risk drive the amount and type of work.

options: Risk of material misstatement and detection risk
mcqs.explain: RMM = inherent × control. In practice: detection risk controllable.

mcqs.q: For significant risks, the auditor must perform:
options: Substantive procedures specifically responsive to the risk
mcqs.explain: SA 330. In practice: plus controls if relying.

mcqs.q: Segregation of duties is part of:
mcqs.explain: Prevents errors and fraud. In practice: authorise, record, custody separated.

remember: Substantive procedures always for significant risks.
traps: Relying on controls without testing them.

viva.model: Misstatements are material if, alone or together, they could reasonably influence users' economic decisions.
Audit risk equals inherent risk times control risk times detection risk.

viva.q: Name the five components of internal control.
viva.model: Control environment, risk assessment, information system and communication, control activities and monitoring.
Written communication of significant deficiencies in internal control to those charged with governance on a timely basis.
An amount below overall materiality used to reduce the risk that total uncorrected and undetected misstatements exceed materiality.

cases.title: Ruby Textiles Ltd.
cases.case: Ruby Textiles had revenue of ₹200 crore and a small loss this year. The auditor chose 1% of revenue as overall materiality. The CFO can approve and release payments alone. Internal audit reported weaknesses that management ignored.

mcqs.explain: 200 × 1%. In practice: revenue benchmark in loss years.

mcqs.q: CFO approving and releasing payments alone is a weakness in:
mcqs.explain: Control activity. In practice: dual authorisation.
mcqs.topic: Internal control: nature, components and limitations

mcqs.q: Ignoring internal audit findings reflects weakness in:
mcqs.explain: No follow-up. In practice: communicate to TCWG.
mcqs.topic: Internal control: nature, components and limitations

mcqs.q: These weaknesses, if significant, are communicated under:
mcqs.explain: In writing to TCWG. In practice: also management letter.
